title: Kingdom of Imereti
capsule: The Kingdom of Imereti emerged as a separate Georgian realm in 1463 following the fragmentation of the unified Kingdom of Georgia, with its capital at Kutaisi in western Transcaucasia. The kingdom occupied a precarious position between Ottoman expansion and Safavid Iran, repeatedly paying tribute to the Ottomans while nominally preserving autonomy; Solomon I (r. 1752–1784) temporarily expelled Ottoman garrisons and won a notable victory at Khresili in 1757. Russian forces occupied Imereti in 1804, and Tsar Alexander I formally abolished the kingdom in 1810, annexing it to the Russian Empire after deposing the last king, Solomon II.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's approximate territory (western Georgia, the Rioni basin) is reasonably well established from Georgian chronicles and Russian imperial surveys, though precise year-by-year boundaries fluctuated with Ottoman pressure and are not mapped in detail.
